title: Spread density of an open in ordinary fibres
statement: Let $f:X\to T$ be a finite type morphism of schemes [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], $W\subset X$ an open subset, and $\eta$ a point with closure all of $T$. For the scheme fibres [def-pc-scheme-fibre] and their canonical maps $i_t:X_t\to X$, suppose $i_\eta^{-1}(W)$ is dense in $X_\eta$. Then there is an open $U\subset T$ containing $\eta$ such that $i_t^{-1}(W)$ is dense in $X_t$ for every $t\in U$. Density means that the topological closure is the entire fibre; empty fibres are allowed. No geometric irreducibility is assumed, and the conclusion concerns ordinary residue-field fibres only.

source.place: Tag 054X, Lemma 37.24.3, applied to the closed complement of an open subset; Tags 03HV and 054U in its proof.

proof.text: Use the nilradical subschemes of X and T. Their closed immersions are surjective embeddings and thus homeomorphisms. The reduced source map factors explicitly through the reduced base by liftNilradical. Transport the generic point using the base embedding specialization equivalence; its existence makes the reduced base integral. The factor map is locally of finite type and quasi-compact by cancellation against the reduction closed immersion. Construct the reduced closed complement of the inverse image of W using Scheme.Opens.closedComplement. Fibre density is preserved by the explicit homeomorphisms obtained from Scheme.Hom.fiberHomeo and restriction of the source homeomorphism to set-theoretic fibres.

Apply generic flat finite presentation to the reduced source map and to its closed-complement map. Both nonempty opens contain the generic point. Intersect them and transport flatness and local finite presentation to the intersection using morphismRestrictRestrict and locality at the target.

The range of the constructed closed complement is the complement of the open. Convert generic density to empty interior using interior_eq_empty_iff_dense_compl. Apply the flat closed-fibre interior theorem on the chosen intersection and convert its conclusion back to density.

Take the image of the intersection open under the reduced-base homeomorphism. This is an open containing the original generic point. For each point in its image, transport the density conclusion from its preimage point using the already proved fibre homeomorphism equivalence. Empty fibres are covered by the same equivalence and complement calculation.

proof_origin.place: Tag 054X, closed-complement proof; source and base nilradical subschemes replace the base-change reduction without changing fibre topology. The preparation and transport steps are proved in Lean; the dimension contradiction is isolated.

lean.statement:
theorem exists_open_fibre_dense_of_generic_dense {X T : Scheme.{u}}
    (f : X ⟶ T) [LocallyOfFiniteType f] [QuasiCompact f]
    (W : X.Opens) (η : T) (hη : IsGenericPoint η Set.univ)
    (hdense : Dense ((f.fiberι η) ⁻¹' (W : Set X))) :
    ∃ U : T.Opens, η ∈ U ∧
      ∀ (t : T), t ∈ U → Dense ((f.fiberι t) ⁻¹' (W : Set X))
